level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa written Order na inilalabas ng Commissioner, District Collector, o awtorisadong customs officer pagkatapos ng Lodgement of Goods Declaration at bago ang actual release ng goods, batay sa Derogatory Information?
level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 3.2, ang Alert Order ay written Order na inilalabas pagkatapos ng Lodgement at bago ang actual release mula sa customs custody, batay sa Derogatory Information tungkol sa posibleng non-compliance.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang calendar days mula sa discharge ng last package dapat i-lodge ang goods declaration?
level1.reason: Sec. 5.5: dapat i-lodge ang goods declaration sa loob ng fifteen (15) calendar days mula sa date ng discharge ng last package mula sa vessel o aircraft.

level1.question: Magkano ang FOB o FCA value ng goods of commercial nature na dapat i-enter sa pamamagitan ng goods declaration for consumption sa ilalim ng Formal Entry Process?
level1.reason: Sec. 5.7.1: ang goods of commercial nature na may FOB o FCA value na Fifty Thousand Pesos (Php50,000.00) and above ay i-eenter sa goods declaration for consumption at i-clear sa Formal Entry Process.

level1.question: Alin ang tama tungkol sa responsibilidad ng Customs Broker sa goods declaration?

choices.A: Responsable siya sa accuracy ng goods declaration at sa payment ng duties, taxes at other charges
choices.B: Hindi siya responsable sa accuracy, pero responsable siya sa payment ng duties at taxes
choices.C: Responsable siya sa accuracy ng goods declaration, pero hindi sa payment ng duties, taxes at other charges
choices.D: Hindi siya responsable sa accuracy at hindi rin sa payment ng duties at taxes

level1.reason: Sec. 5.3: ang Customs Broker ay responsable rin sa accuracy ng goods declaration, pero hindi siya responsable sa payment ng duties, taxes at other charges. Ang declarant ang responsable sa payment.

level1.question: Sa provisional goods declaration, ilang calendar days mula sa lodgement ang unang palugit para isumite ang iba pang supporting documents ayon sa notarized undertaking ng declarant?
level1.reason: Sec. 5.7.5.b.iv: ang notarized undertaking ay nagsasabing isusumite ang ibang documents sa loob ng forty-five (45) calendar days mula lodgement, na puwedeng i-extend ng another 45 calendar days para sa valid reasons.

level1.question: Magkano ang legal interest per annum sa unpaid duties, taxes at other charges ayon sa CAO?
level1.reason: Sec. 8.6: ang unpaid duties, taxes at other charges ay may legal interest na twenty per cent (20%) per annum, computed mula sa date ng final assessment.

level1.question: Kung walang fraud at ang goods ay finally assessed at released na, pagkalipas ng ilang taon mula sa date ng final payment of duties and taxes (o completion ng post clearance audit) nagiging conclusive ang assessment sa lahat ng parties?
level1.reason: Sec. 9.3 (Period of Limitation): sa absence of fraud, conclusive na ang assessment sa lahat ng parties three (3) years mula final payment ng duties and taxes, o pagkatapos ng post clearance audit.

level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang hindi tatanggapin ng AAB bilang payment ng customs duties at taxes?

choices.B: Cash payment sa pamamagitan ng debit mula sa nominated account ng importer sa AAB

level1.reason: Sec. 8.2.2.a: ang AABs ay hindi tatanggap ng TCCs bilang payment ng customs duties at taxes. Ang TDM at DPGA ay nakalista bilang non-cash modes, at ang cash debit ay nasa Sec. 8.2.1.

level1.question: Ayon sa Rule 3(c) ng General Rules for the Interpretation (GRI), saang heading ima-classify ang goods na hindi ma-classify ayon sa Rule 3(a) o 3(b)?

choices.A: Sa heading na last in numerical order sa mga heading na equally merit consideration
choices.B: Sa heading na first in numerical order sa mga heading na equally merit consideration
choices.C: Sa heading na appropriate sa goods na pinaka-akin dito
choices.D: Sa heading na nagbibigay ng essential character ng goods

level1.reason: Sec. 4.11.3.c (Rule 3(c)): kapag hindi ma-classify ang goods sa 3(a) o 3(b), ima-classify ito sa heading na occurs last in numerical order among those which equally merit consideration.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa Method Three sa Methods of Valuation?
level1.reason: Sec. 4.9.4: ang Transaction Value of Similar Goods ay Method Three. Ang Method Two ay Identical Goods (Sec. 4.9.3), Method Four ay Deductive Value (Sec. 4.9.5), at Method Five ay Computed Value (Sec. 4.9.6).

level2.question: Luzon Trading Corp. is the importer of a shipment whose last package was discharged from the vessel on 1 June. On 12 June, before the 15-day period to lodge expired, its broker submitted a written request to extend the period, citing a valid ground (an accident). The Collector of Customs did not act on the request within seven working days. What is the status of the request and the extension period?

choices.A: The request is deemed denied, and the importer may only lodge a provisional goods declaration.
choices.B: The request remains pending until the Commissioner acts, and the original period continues to run.
choices.C: The request is deemed approved, and the extra 15 calendar days begin on the day immediately after the original period expired.
choices.D: The request is deemed approved, and the extra 15 calendar days begin on the date the request was filed.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.5, a written request filed before the original period expires and based on a valid ground (accident is listed) may extend the period by another 15 calendar days. If not acted upon within seven (7) working days, the request is deemed approved, and the extension retroacts to the day immediately after the expiration of the original period.

level2.question: Harbor Foods Inc. lodged a provisional goods declaration for regulated goods because its import permit had not yet been issued, although it timely applied for it. The regulatory agency allows conditional release. Harbor Foods is not enrolled in any trade facilitation program of the Bureau. Which conditions apply to the conditional release of the goods?

choices.A: The goods must be delivered to the importer's premises for storage and not be disposed of until the permit is issued and submitted, and a specific and sufficient security must be posted.
choices.B: The goods may be freely disposed of, and only a general security or an undertaking is required.
choices.C: The goods must stay in the Bureau's custody, and no security is required because the permit was timely applied for.
choices.D: The goods may be released only after the permit is issued, because regulated goods cannot be conditionally released.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.7.5.d.i, for regulated shipments the agency must allow the release; the goods are delivered to the importer's premises for storage and not disposed of until the permit is issued and submitted, and a specific and sufficient security is required. A general security or undertaking applies only to importers enrolled in trade facilitation programs, which Harbor Foods is not.

level2.question: A shipment of electronics was electronically selected for physical examination. After due notice, the declarant, Mr. Reyes, failed to appear at the scheduled examination. What should the Bureau do?

choices.A: Postpone the examination until Mr. Reyes appears, since his presence is mandatory.
choices.B: Proceed under the authority of the Collector of Customs, inform the Office of the Commissioner and concerned offices of the date, time and place, and ensure the entire proceeding is captured on video.
choices.C: Proceed only after the Commissioner approves a controlled delivery in writing.
choices.D: Proceed only at the consignee's warehouse, without the need to inform the Office of the Commissioner.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 6.4.4.a, examination in the declarant's absence is allowed when, despite due notice, the declarant fails to be physically present. It is under the authority of the Collector, the Office of the Commissioner and concerned offices must be informed of the date, time and place, and the entire proceeding must be captured on video.

level2.question: Pacific Gadgets Inc. imports goods from Sunrise Ltd. Mr. Tan directly owns six percent (6%) of the outstanding voting shares of both companies. The Bureau questions whether the declared transaction value may be used. How should the transaction value be treated under the CAO?

choices.A: It is automatically rejected because the buyer and seller are related.
choices.B: It is automatically accepted because related persons are covered only if they own 50% or more of the shares.
choices.C: It is replaced by the deductive value, because sales between related persons cannot use Method One.
choices.D: It may be accepted if the importer demonstrates that it closely approximates one of the stated test values occurring at or about the same time.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 4.9.2, persons are deemed related if any person owns, controls or holds five percent (5%) or more of the voting shares of both seller and buyer, so the parties are related. In a sale between related persons, the transaction value is accepted whenever the importer demonstrates that it closely approximates a stated test value, such as the transaction value in sales to unrelated buyers of identical or similar goods, or the deductive or computed value.

level2.question: Metro Steel's imported goods are stored in a warehouse. The duty rate under the applicable tariff heading changed on 1 September. Metro Steel lodged its goods declaration for consumption on 28 August, and the goods were physically withdrawn on 3 September. Which duty rate applies?

choices.A: The rate effective on 28 August, the date of lodgement of the goods declaration for consumption.
choices.B: The rate effective on 3 September, the date of physical withdrawal.
choices.C: The lower of the rates before and after 1 September.
choices.D: The rate effective on the date the Final Assessment Notice is issued.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 4.14, goods are subject to the rate effective upon withdrawal from the warehouse for consumption, which the CAO states means upon lodgement of the goods declaration for consumption. Lodgement was on 28 August, so the rate effective on that date applies.

level2.question: Dela Cruz Imports cannot present the original Bill of Lading for its shipment, but the carrier's agent issued a written order for the delivery of the goods to the company. What may the customs officer do?

choices.A: Refuse to clear the goods until the original BL is produced, since no clearance is allowed without it under any circumstance.
choices.B: Clear the goods only if the importer posts a security equal to the value of the goods.
choices.C: Clear the goods against the carrier's written order, but require the submission of a copy of the bill.
choices.D: Clear the goods against the carrier's written order without requiring a copy of the bill, because the order replaces it.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 9.1.2, no customs officer shall clear goods for delivery without the BL or AWB, except on written order of the carrier or agent of the vessel or aircraft. When clearance is made against such written order, the customs officer shall require the submission of a copy of the bill.

level2.question: On 1 October, an Authorized Agent Bank received a payment instruction from the Bureau for an importer's shipment. The importer's debit account lacked sufficient balance, so the bank transmitted no payment confirmation. By 20 October, there was still no confirmation. What is the consequence?

choices.A: The goods declaration is automatically cancelled, and the importer must lodge a new one.
choices.B: The Bureau automatically extends the payment period by another 15 calendar days.
choices.C: The Bureau must issue a new Final Assessment Notice to the importer.
choices.D: The importer is deemed to have failed to claim the importation after lodging the goods declaration, making the goods liable to abandonment.

level2.reason: Under Secs. 8.4 and 8.5, the AAB transmits a payment confirmation unless the debit account has insufficient balance. If no confirmation is received within fifteen (15) calendar days from the AAB's receipt of the payment instruction, the importer is deemed to have failed to claim the importation, rendering it liable to abandonment. Here, 19 days passed without confirmation.

level2.question: Bayview Corp.'s final assessment under Section 7.3 shows duties and taxes of Php500,000. Payment became due and demandable on the date of final assessment, but Bayview paid exactly one year later. Disregarding any fine or penalty, how much legal interest accrued?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 8.6, unpaid duties and taxes incur legal interest of 20% per annum from the date of final assessment. Php500,000 x 20% x 1 year = Php100,000.

level2.question: A company imports garments packed in ordinary cartons of a kind normally used for packing such garments. The cartons are not clearly suitable for repetitive use. Under the GRI rules in the CAO, how are the cartons classified?

choices.A: Separately, under their own heading, because packing materials are distinct goods.
choices.B: Under the heading which occurs last in numerical order among those which equally merit consideration.
choices.C: Together with the garments, because they are of a kind normally used for packing such goods.
choices.D: Under the heading appropriate to the goods to which the cartons are most akin.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 4.11.5.b (Rule 5(b)), packing materials and containers presented with the goods are classified with the goods if they are of a kind normally used for packing such goods, except when clearly suitable for repetitive use. The cartons meet the first condition and not the exception.

level2.question: A consignment arrives for Alpha Corp., which is enrolled in a trade facilitation program of the Bureau. A District Collector suspects forged documents and believes an Alert Order is warranted. Who may issue the Alert Order, and where is physical examination conducted?

choices.A: The District Collector, with physical examination at the pier.
choices.B: Any customs officer authorized in writing by the Commissioner, with physical examination at the port facility.
choices.C: The Commissioner or the District Collector, with physical examination at a facility chosen by the Bureau.
choices.D: Only the Commissioner, with physical examination at the consignee's warehouse or premises, subject to conditions imposed by the Bureau.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 11, valuation issues from forged or spurious documents are subject to Alert Orders. When the importation is consigned to an importer enrolled in a trade facilitation program, only the Commissioner may issue an Alert Order, and physical examination is conducted at the consignee's warehouse or premises subject to conditions imposed by the Bureau.
